title: SOAP-Bubbles ◦❍ Structured Weight Uncertainty for Neural Networks
claim: Structured posteriors from a cheap preconditioner fit the true distribution better than diagonal ones, and also train faster and predict better.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, shared red-vs-gray color coding across panels
description: Three side-by-side panels, with red for the proposed method and gray for the baseline throughout. The left panel is a 2-D sketch titled 'SOAP-Bubbles > Diagonal'. A gray axis-aligned ellipse labeled 'Diagonal Covariance' is turned by an arrow ('SOAP's Precond.') into a tilted red ellipse, the 'SOAP Bubble'. Both ellipses are drawn inside a large black triangular outline, the exact posterior. The red ellipse sits closer to the posterior's mass than the gray one, and a star marks the MAP. The middle panel is a line plot for NanoGPT-123M-FineWeb1B. It plots validation loss against time in hours, with EVON in red below IVON in gray and a zoom inset at the end of the curves. The right panel is titled 'Test-Time Posterior Sampling'. It plots perplexity improvement against the number of MC samples, and the red curve rises well above the gray one. The eye goes first to the red elements.
caption: Our key idea is to use SOAP's preconditioner to transform diagonal covariances into non-diagonal ones. We call the resulting posteriors SOAP-Bubbles and \revision{show that} they provide a much better fit to the exact posterior \revision{(left)}. Our new optimizer EVON runs the state-of-the-art variational method IVON in SOAP's eigenspace and significantly improves both the training speed and final loss for language models \revision{(middle)}. SOAP-Bubble posteriors obtained with EVON also work much better for model averaging during test-time than IVON's diagonal posteriors \revision{(right)}.
abstract: Structured weight-uncertainty can improve many aspects of deep learning, but it remains costly to estimate and difficult to implement. Here, we show that these issues can be addressed by adapting the SOAP optimizer. Our key idea is to run IVON, an existing diagonal-covariance variational method, in the eigenspace of SOAP's preconditioner and then use the preconditioner to transform the diagonal estimate into a non-diagonal covariance. The resulting method has costs similar to those of SOAP and requires no drastic changes to training pipelines. We call the posteriors obtained in this way SOAP-Bubbles and our new optimizer Eigenspace-VON (EVON). We show that, for logistic regression, EVON can match the full Gaussian covariance and that, for language model pretraining, it yields significantly better results than existing diagonal-covariance methods. Our work makes it easier to estimate more expressive posterior distributions for deep learning at scale.
